title: Compiler Arithmetic Semantic Preservation (Source → IR → Bytecode)

academic_terms: observational equivalence of source and target

descriptions.semantic: For every source program, the bytecode the compiler emits exhibits the same observable arithmetic behaviour as the source-level semantics: a checked operation that overflows/underflows at source level reverts in the emitted code under exactly the same conditions; operand widths and signedness are preserved; and no optimization pass silently introduces wrap-around, reordering, or strength-reduction that changes a result or a revert condition. Compilation is also deterministic (same input → same bytecode).
descriptions.system_theoretic: A forward (and ideally backward) simulation between the source-level transition system and the target (EVM) transition system: there exists a relation R between source and target states, preserved by stepping, such that related states produce equivalent observable arithmetic events. Restricted here to the arithmetic fragment of the full compiler-correctness statement.
descriptions.security: Downstream value-safety properties (no-unauthorized-mint, conservation) are stated and verified at the source level but EXECUTE as bytecode. If the compiler does not preserve arithmetic semantics, a source-level proof of 'this cannot overflow' is vacuous against the deployed artifact. This property is the bridge that lets source-level assurance transfer to on-chain behaviour.
descriptions.execution_semantics: Solidity ≥0.8 emits explicit overflow/underflow checks (revert) for checked arithmetic; `unchecked{}` blocks and inline assembly opt out. The optimizer (legacy + Yul/IR pipeline) rewrites code; a miscompilation is an optimizer transformation that is not semantics-preserving (e.g. eliding a check, mis-modeling a cleanup, mis-handling a corner constant).
descriptions.formal_verification: Established by (a) a once-and-for-all proof of compiler correctness in a proof assistant (CompCert paradigm), rarely available for production EVM compilers, or more practically (b) TRANSLATION VALIDATION per compilation: prove the specific source and the specific emitted bytecode are equivalent (symbolic equivalence / SMT), and (c) differential testing against a reference semantics. It is computationally conditional because full equivalence is undecidable in general; per-program bounded equivalence is tractable.

formalization.signature: ⟦·⟧_src : Program → (Input → Behaviour); compile : Program → Bytecode; ⟦·⟧_evm : Bytecode → (Input → Behaviour); Behaviour includes return value, revert, and gas-relevant observables.
formalization.first_order_logic:
Semantic preservation (arithmetic fragment):  ∀ P, in . ⟦P⟧_src(in) ≈_arith ⟦compile(P)⟧_evm(in),  where ≈_arith equates results and revert-on-overflow conditions for arithmetic operations.
Determinism:  ∀ P . compile(P) is a function (same flags ⇒ identical bytes).

hoare.pre: source op a+b with a+b > MAX (checked)

formalization.state_machine: Product of source and target machines with a simulation relation R; the property is that R is a (forward) simulation: related states step to related states with equivalent arithmetic observables.
formalization.type_theoretic: Type preservation + a logical relation: well-typed source of integer type Tₙ compiles to target operations respecting Tₙ's width; the logical relation at integer type relates values that are equal modulo the (preserved) width discipline.
formalization.algebraic: Source checked-arithmetic is the partial operation on ℤ that is undefined (reverts) outside [0, 2ⁿ); the target must implement the SAME partial operation, not the total mod-2ⁿ ring operation.

relationships.note: Storage-layout preservation is the sibling compiler-correctness fragment for state, not arithmetic.

attack_surface.pattern: an optimizer pass elides a bounds check or mis-rewrites arithmetic, changing results or revert behaviour
incident_refs: Solidity compiler known-bugs list (Yul optimizer / cleanup / constant-folding classes) — VERIFY specific entries before citing
attack_surface.notes: Argues for pinning compiler versions and re-validating on upgrade.

attack_surface.pattern: developer-elided checks in unchecked{}/assembly reintroduce wrap; preservation holds but the spec the developer relied on does not
attack_surface.notes: Property preserved; the WRONG source semantics was chosen. Cross-ref BPO:0001 assumption.

attack_surface.pattern: metadata/path/flag nondeterminism yields differing bytecode, breaking verifiable builds
attack_surface.notes: Deterministic compilation is part of this property.

metrics: differential-test divergence count (compiled vs reference semantics)
invariant_checkpoints: per-release: emitted checks present for all checked ops
runtime_assertions: on-chain: redundant post-condition asserts as defense-in-depth

strategies.notes: Symbolically prove source-derived and emitted bytecode agree on the arithmetic fragment for a given program.
Random programs/inputs compared against a trusted semantics; finds optimizer regressions.
Strongest but seldom available for production EVM toolchains.

testability: overflow at source ⇒ revert in deployed bytecode
optimizer on/off observationally equivalent on arithmetic

runtime: redundant on-chain assertions for critical arithmetic (defense-in-depth)
static: pin and hash compiler version + flags
re-run translation validation on compiler upgrade
design_patterns: prefer checked arithmetic; isolate and audit unchecked{}/assembly

assumptions.statement: The reference EVM semantics used for validation faithfully models the deployed client's execution.
The compiler binary used is the audited/pinned one (supply-chain integrity).

sources: Leroy, Formal verification of a realistic compiler (CompCert)
provenance.notes: Primary discharge target for the arithmetic assumption of BPO:0001. Storage-layout preservation tracked separately under BPO:0030.
